title: Seetha shows the gifts of Anasuya to Rama
introduction: As the evening twilight approaches, Anasuya sends Seetha to Rama's presence. Seetha approaches Rama and shows him the apparel, jewels and garlands gifted by Anasuya and duly adorned by her, Rama spends the night there along with Seetha Lakshmana. At the onset of dawn, they take leave of the ascetics and advance further into the great forest in the route suggested by the ascetics.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीये चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रिकायाम् संहितायां श्रीमदयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनविंशत्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः
Thus completes 119th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
अनसूया तु धर्मज्ना श्रुत्वा ताम् महतीम् कथाम् |
पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्याम् शिरस्य् आघ्राय मैथिलीम्
verses.iast:
anasūyā tu dharmajnā śrutvā tām mahatīm kathām |
paryaṣvajata bāhubhyām śirasy āghrāya maithilīm
verses.translation: Hearing that great story, Anasuya the knower of piety kissed Seetha's forehead and hugged her in her arms.

verses.devanagari:
व्यक्त अक्षर पदम् चित्रम् भाषितम् मधुरम् त्वया |
यथा स्वयम् वरम् वृत्तम् तत् सर्वम् हि श्रुतम् मया
रमे अहम् कथया ते तु दृष्ढम् मधुर भाषिणि |
verses.iast:
vyakta akṣara padam citram bhāṣitam madhuram tvayā |
yathā svayam varam vṛttam tat sarvam hi śrutam mayā
rame aham kathayā te tu dṛṣḍham madhura bhāṣiṇi |
verses.translation: "It was narrated sweetly and amazingly by you, in clear words and syllables. It has been indeed heard by me how all that Svayamvara, the process of self-choosing marriage took place. O, the sweet speaking Seetha! I am overjoyed by hearing your story."

verses.devanagari:
रविर् अस्तम् गतः श्रीमान् उपोह्य रजनीम् शिवाम्
दिवसम् प्रति कीर्णानाम् आहार अर्थम् पतत्रिणाम् |
संध्या काले निलीनानाम् निद्रा अर्थम् श्रूयते ध्वनिः
verses.iast:
ravir astam gataḥ śrīmān upohya rajanīm śivām
divasam prati kīrṇānām āhāra artham patatriṇām |
saṃdhyā kāle nilīnānām nidrā artham śrūyate dhvaniḥ
verses.translation: "O, Fortunate One! While the auspicious night drawing near, the sun has sunk below horizon. The twittering of the birds can be heard, who, through the day, have sought their nourishment far and wide and are seeking their shelter for sleep at the time of evening-twilight."

verses.devanagari:
एते च अप्य् अभिषेक आर्द्रा मुनयः फल शोधनाः |
सहिता उपवर्तन्ते सलिल आप्लुत वल्कलाः
verses.iast:
ete ca apy abhiṣeka ārdrā munayaḥ phala śodhanāḥ |
sahitā upavartante salila āpluta valkalāḥ
verses.translation: "These ascetics too are returning together, their bark-robes drenched from bathing, and with uplifted vessels, wet with sprinkled water on them."

glosses.meaning: their bark = robes drenched from bathing

verses.devanagari:
ऋषीणाम् अग्नि होत्रेषु हुतेषु विधि पुर्वकम् |
कपोत अन्ग अरुणो धूमो दृश्यते पवन उद्धतः
verses.iast:
ṛṣīṇām agni hotreṣu huteṣu vidhi purvakam |
kapota anga aruṇo dhūmo dṛśyate pavana uddhataḥ
verses.translation: "From the sacred fire kindled by the sages, according to the scriptural ordinance, a column of smoke with the hue of a Pigeon's neck, raised by the wind, is seen there."

glosses.meaning: with the hue of a pigeon's neck

verses.devanagari:
अल्प पर्णा हि तरवो घनी भूताः समन्ततः |
विप्रकृष्टे अपि ये देशे न प्रकाशन्ति वै दिशः
verses.iast:
alpa parṇā hi taravo ghanī bhūtāḥ samantataḥ |
viprakṛṣṭe api ye deśe na prakāśanti vai diśaḥ
verses.translation: "Thought their foliage is sparse, the trees look dense all around. The quarters of the world, by whom the senses are drawn apart, do not shine brilliantly at this place."

glosses.meaning: by whom the senses are drawn apart.

verses.devanagari:
रजनी रस सत्त्वानि प्रचरन्ति समन्ततः |
तपो वन मृगा ह्य् एते वेदि तीर्थेषु शेरते
verses.iast:
rajanī rasa sattvāni pracaranti samantataḥ |
tapo vana mṛgā hy ete vedi tīrtheṣu śerate
verses.translation: "The animals who wander about at night are ranging everywhere. The deer of the hermitage are sleeping round the sacred altars."

glosses.meaning: the animals who wander about at night

verses.devanagari:
सम्प्रवृत्ता निशा सीते नक्षत्र समलम्कृता |
ज्योत्स्ना प्रावरणः चन्द्रो दृश्यते अभ्युदितो अम्बरे
verses.iast:
sampravṛttā niśā sīte nakṣatra samalamkṛtā |
jyotsnā prāvaraṇaḥ candro dṛśyate abhyudito ambare
verses.translation: "O, Seetha! The night richly adorned with stars has set well in motion. The moon encircled with light is seen rising in the sky."

verses.devanagari:
गम्यताम् अनुजानामि रामस्य अनुचरी भव |
कथयन्त्या हि मधुरम् त्वया अहम् परितोषिता
verses.iast:
gamyatām anujānāmi rāmasya anucarī bhava |
kathayantyā hi madhuram tvayā aham paritoṣitā
verses.translation: "Go now. I give you leave. Be a female companion to Rama. Your sweet conversation has charmed me."

verses.devanagari:
अलम्कुरु च तावत् त्वम् प्रत्यक्षम् मम मैथिलि |
प्रीतिम् जनय मे वत्स दिव्य अलम्काल शोभिनी
verses.iast:
alamkuru ca tāvat tvam pratyakṣam mama maithili |
prītim janaya me vatsa divya alamkāla śobhinī
verses.translation: "O, Seetha! O, Dear child! Adorn (with ornaments and apparel gifted by me_ before my eyes and cause delight to me in embellishing yourself with heavenly jewels."

glosses.meaning: adorn (with ornaments and apparel gifted by me)
in embellishing yourself with heavenly ornaments.

verses.devanagari:
सा तदा समलम्कृत्य सीता सुर सुत उपमा |
प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्यै रामम् तु अभिमुखी ययौ
verses.iast:
sā tadā samalamkṛtya sītā sura suta upamā |
praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmam tu abhimukhī yayau
verses.translation: Then Seetha, adorning herself, resembled the daughter of a god, and making obeisance to the feet of Anasuya, she went forward to meet Rama.

glosses.meaning: similar to the daughter of a god

verses.devanagari:
तथा तु भूषिताम् सीताम् ददर्श वदताम् वरः |
राघवः प्रीति दानेन तपस्विन्या जहर्ष च
verses.iast:
tathā tu bhūṣitām sītām dadarśa vadatām varaḥ |
rāghavaḥ prīti dānena tapasvinyā jaharṣa ca
verses.translation: Rama, the most eloquent one, saw Seetha adorned as aforesaid and felt delighted over the charming gifts of the ascetic.

verses.devanagari:
न्यवेदयत् ततः सर्वम् सीता रामाय मैथिली |
प्रीति दानम् तपस्विन्या वसन आभरण स्रजाम्
verses.iast:
nyavedayat tataḥ sarvam sītā rāmāya maithilī |
prīti dānam tapasvinyā vasana ābharaṇa srajām
verses.translation: Seetha, the daughter of Mithila kingdom then showed to Rama all the apparel, jewels and garlands the affectionate gifts of Anasuya the hermitess.

verses.devanagari:
प्रहृष्टः तु अभवद् रामो लक्ष्मणः च महा रथः |
मैथिल्याः सत्क्रियाम् दृष्ट्वा मानुषेषु सुदुर्लभाम्
verses.iast:
prahṛṣṭaḥ tu abhavad rāmo lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahā rathaḥ |
maithilyāḥ satkriyām dṛṣṭvā mānuṣeṣu sudurlabhām
verses.translation: Seeing the respectful treatment, received by Seetha, which was very rare among human beings, Rama and Lakshmana the great car-warrior felt highly rejoiced.

verses.devanagari:
ततः ताम् सर्वरीम् प्रीतः पुण्याम् शशि निभ आननः |
अर्चितः तापसैः सिद्धैर् उवास रघु नन्दनः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tām sarvarīm prītaḥ puṇyām śaśi nibha ānanaḥ |
arcitaḥ tāpasaiḥ siddhair uvāsa raghu nandanaḥ
verses.translation: Thereupon, Rama with his face resembling the moon, having been honoured by the holy ascetics, was delighted and spent that auspicious night there.

glosses.meaning: with his face resembling the moon

verses.devanagari:
तस्याम् रात्र्याम् व्यतीतायाम् अभिषिच्य हुत अग्निकान् |
आपृग्च्छेताम् नर व्याघ्रौ तापसान् वन गोचरान्
verses.iast:
tasyām rātryām vyatītāyām abhiṣicya huta agnikān |
āpṛgcchetām nara vyāghrau tāpasān vana gocarān
verses.translation: While that night passed away, Rama and Lakshmana the tigers among men finished their ablutions and took leave of the ascetics dwelling the forest, who had just poured oblations into the sacred fire.

glosses.meaning: Rama and Lakshamna the tigers among men
of the ascetics dwelling in the forest
who had just poured oblations into the sacred fire.

verses.devanagari:
ताउ ऊचुः ते वन चराः तापसा धर्म चारिणः |
वनस्य तस्य संचारम् राक्षसैः समभिप्लुतम्
verses.iast:
tāu ūcuḥ te vana carāḥ tāpasā dharma cāriṇaḥ |
vanasya tasya saṃcāram rākṣasaiḥ samabhiplutam
verses.translation: Those ascetics dwelling in the forest and practising virtue told Rama and Lakshmana about the region of that forest, which was infested with demons (as follows):

verses.devanagari:
रक्षांसि पुरुषादानि नानारूपाणि राघव! |
वसन्त्यस्मिन् महारण्ये व्याळाश्चश्च रुधिराशनाः
verses.iast:
rakṣāṃsi puruṣādāni nānārūpāṇi rāghava! |
vasantyasmin mahāraṇye vyāLāścaśca rudhirāśanāḥ
verses.translation: "O, Rama! Various forms of man-eating demons and beasts drinking the blood are living in this great forest."

verses.devanagari:
उच्चिष्टम् वा प्रमत्तम् वा तापसम् धर्मचारिणम् |
अदन्त्यस्मिन् महारण्ये तान्निवारय राघवः
verses.iast:
ucciṣṭam vā pramattam vā tāpasam dharmacāriṇam |
adantyasmin mahāraṇye tānnivāraya rāghavaḥ
verses.translation: "O, Rama! They devour an ascetic or a celibate, who has not rinsed his mouth after finishing his meal or who is inattentive in this great forest. (Pray ward them off!"

glosses.meaning: who has not rinsed his mouth after finishing his meal

verses.devanagari:
एष पन्था महर्षीणाम् फलान्य् आहरताम् वने |
अनेन तु वनम् दुर्गम् गन्तुम् राघव ते क्षमम्
verses.iast:
eṣa panthā maharṣīṇām phalāny āharatām vane |
anena tu vanam durgam gantum rāghava te kṣamam
verses.translation: "O, Rama! Here is the path of the great sages, through which they fetch the fruits in this forest. It is appropriate for you to go by this path in this dangerous forest."

verses.devanagari:
इति इव तैः प्रान्जलिभिः तपस्विभिर्
र्द्विजैः कृत स्वस्त्ययनः परम् तपः |
वनम् सभार्यः प्रविवेश राघवः |
सलक्ष्मणः सूर्य इव अभ्र मण्डलम्
verses.iast:
iti iva taiḥ prānjalibhiḥ tapasvibhir
rdvijaiḥ kṛta svastyayanaḥ param tapaḥ |
vanam sabhāryaḥ praviveśa rāghavaḥ |
salakṣmaṇaḥ sūrya iva abhra maṇḍalam
verses.translation: Thus addressed by those Brahmanas having great asceticism, who, with joined palms paid obedience to him and blessed his journey, Rama the harasser of his foes entered the forest with his consort along with Lakshmana, as sun enters a mass of clouds.

glosses.meaning: paid obedience to him and blessed his journey
